title: Types of Redox Reactions Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Lego bricks snap together or break apart, and a stronger player can take another player's place. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 7, Redox Reactions) Aarav waits in the corridor before his test with twenty reactions to sort, and we find the four families every redox reaction belongs to.

You will learn the redox check (one oxidation number up, another down), then see combination (C + O2 -> CO2), decomposition (water split by electricity) and why heating CaCO3 is not redox. On the molecule bench chlorine bubbles into potassium bromide, snatches electrons from bromide and turns the solution orange: halogen displacement, with F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2. We walk the metal activity series, metal and hydrogen displacement, disproportionation (Cl2 in cold alkali) and comproportionation (2H2S + SO2 -> 3S + 2H2O), compare decomposition with disproportionation, sort four reactions in a worked example, show the decomposition trap, then an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 73 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Join, break, swap: redox families
0:26 Is it redox? The oxidation number check
0:43 Combination and decomposition
1:17 Displacement on the molecule bench: Cl2 into KBr
1:48 The activity series and hydrogen displacement
2:20 Disproportionation and comproportionation
2:50 Decomposition vs disproportionation
3:29 Worked example: sort four reactions
4:12 Exam trap: not every decomposition is redox
4:33 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:05 Recap and three questions to answer
